sourceFile: PDF fetched directly from https://iowaepiscopal.squarespace.com/s/2026-Joint-Intercession-List.pdf ("2026 Joint Intercession List", Dioceses of Iowa, Brechin, Eswatini, and Nzara), linked from https://iowaepiscopal.squarespace.com/intercession.
notes: This PDF ("2026 Joint Intercession List") is a single joint monthly cycle shared by four dioceses -- Iowa and its three companion dioceses: The Diocese of Brechin (the Scottish Episcopal Church), The Diocese of Eswatini (the Anglican Church of Southern Africa), and The Diocese of Nzara (the Episcopal Church of South Sudan) -- printed side by side under headings "(B)", "(E)", "(I)", and "(N)" for each day of the month, with no calendar year given anywhere in the source. This confirms cycleType 'monthly-recurring'. This file records only the Diocese of Iowa's own cycle (scope 'diocese'): Iowa's own "(I)" items become `parish`/`category` subjects, while each day's Brechin/Eswatini/Nzara companion-diocese content is recorded as `category` subjects rather than `parish`, per this corpus's standing convention for companion-diocese items (see episcopal-chicago-2026.json). Each companion-diocese subject's `name` is tagged "(Companion Diocese of Brechin/Eswatini/Nzara)", matching the Chicago file's own "(Companion Diocese of X)" convention. The companion dioceses' own full monthly cycles are not separate corpus files -- only what this source prints for them alongside Iowa each day is captured here.
The source's own front matter (p. 3) names this diocese only as "The Diocese of Iowa", not "The Episcopal Diocese of Iowa"; transcribed exactly as printed.

Verified this is a genuine single-column, day-of-month 1-31 layout (not a multi-column grid at risk of interleaving) by rendering 9 of the PDF's 31-day pages (pp. 4-12, covering all 31 days) as images and visually comparing them against the linearized `pdftotext -layout` extraction before transcribing; no column-interleaving or misassignment was found, though a few small deviations from a naive text extraction were caught this way (see below).

Splitting methodology: each day's (I)/(B)/(E)/(N) text is split into multiple subjects only where the source clearly delimits separate named parishes/parochial districts/offices as distinct "Name, Place: detail" segments joined by semicolons (mirroring how Iowa's own multi-congregation days are split). A paragraph that names one topic/body with subsidiary detail and no repeated "Name:" delimiter is kept as a single subject with the full text preserved in `note`, following this corpus's existing convention (episcopal-northern-indiana.json) of semicolon-joining multi-item lists into `note` rather than fragmenting into many subjects. Eswatini's day 30 item names several diocesan bodies (Diocesan Trust Board, Diocesan Executive Committee/Finance, the Cathedral Chapter, The Council of Swaziland Churches, Board of Education, Board of Social Development) without a repeated delimiter between them; these were lumped into one category subject led by the first-named body ("Diocesan Trust Board"), with the rest preserved verbatim in `note`, rather than guessing at a further split the source does not clearly mark.

Day 2's source prints a stray duplicate heading "Day 2" immediately before that day's "(N)" line -- confirmed on the rendered page image, not a text-extraction artifact -- and was excluded from the transcription since the entry is already keyed by `day: 2`.
Day 31 has no "(E)" Eswatini item at all -- confirmed both in the text extraction and the rendered page image -- transcribed as printed, with nothing fabricated for that slot.

Three Iowa items printed in the same "Name, Place:" pattern as parish entries were instead recorded as `category` rather than `parish`, as a judgment call: "Old Brick, Iowa City" (day 10, a community ministry/nonprofit operating out of a former church building, not itself an active congregation), and "Beloved Community Initiative" and "Agape Café" (day 10, named ministries printed with no place).

Day 18's "Trinity Cluster: St Paul, Harlan; Trinity, Denison; & Trinity, Carroll: Diana Wright" is transcribed as three separate `parish` subjects (St Paul/Harlan, Trinity/Denison, Trinity/Carroll), each noting "Trinity Cluster" and the last carrying the shared leader "Diana Wright" exactly where the source places it.

Day 12's "Church of the Good Shepherd, Webster City and Grace, Boone: Catherine Schroeder" and day 22's "St Alban, Spirit Lake and All Saints, Storm Lake: Carolyn Tuttle" are each transcribed as two separate `parish` subjects sharing the same named leader, since the source names two distinct congregations joined by "and" under one shared person.

Day 11's Iowa item "Trinity Cush, Des Moines" is preserved exactly as printed (confirmed against the rendered page image) even though it may be a typo for another name (e.g. "Trinity Church") -- not silently corrected.

A handful of apparent source typos/oddities are preserved verbatim rather than corrected: day 3's Eswatini item ends with a stray trailing comma ("...Revd. Petros Dlamini,"); day 22's Nzara item has a duplicated word ("Revd. Revd. Canon Keliopa Elisa"); day 23's Eswatini item has a right double-quotation-mark character in a name where an apostrophe would be expected ("Thab”sile Masuku"); day 31's Nzara item punctuates its second parish with a semicolon rather than a colon ("Navundio Parish; Revd. Joseph Taban") -- all transcribed as printed.
